review.body: 🎟️ claim-link onboarding for approved minors reads clean, ship it.

The relay `message` listener starts the underage-user case creation in a detached promise, so that work can be lost if the Durable Object is reset, hibernated, or evicted before it finishes. That would leave an underage-user report with no age-review case, so it needs to be fixed before this can merge. Attach the work to the object's lifecycle or a durable queue before the listener returns, and add a regression test that pins the behavior. The rest of the change looks solid.

comment.body:
This listener kicks off the age-review work and then returns, so nothing keeps the Durable Object alive until that work finishes.

The awaits you added downstream are correct. The `NS-underageUser` branch in `handleReportEvent` awaits `createAgeReviewCase` (ReportWatcher.ts:634), so the Keycast and D1 writes are properly sequenced. The problem is one level up. This callback calls `this.handleMessage(...).catch(...)` and returns immediately, so the whole chain runs in a detached promise. If the object is reset, hibernated, or evicted before that promise settles, the case creation is lost and the underage-user report ends up with no age-review case.

Attach the work to the object's lifecycle before the callback returns. The lightweight fix is to pass the promise to `this.state.waitUntil(...)` so the runtime waits for it. The durable fix, which also survives hibernation and eviction, is to persist the report to storage or an alarm here and run the Keycast and D1 work from there.

Keep the `pendingAgeReviewPubkeys` guard, or swap it for a durable idempotency key if you move to a queue. Add a regression test that proves an `NS-underageUser` message is not treated as fully processed until the case-creation path is attached to the lifecycle or durably queued.

Validate `verified_minor` before using it to auto-clear an age-review case.
`getUserStatus` currently passes untyped Keycast JSON through to `ReportWatcher`, where any truthy value clears the report.
A response like `"false"` or `1` would skip normal review for an underage-user report.
Decode the response at runtime and only treat `verified_minor === true` as approved; malformed or missing values should fall through to the normal open case path, with tests for `"false"`, `1`, missing, and `true`.

review.body:
This PR needs changes before merge because the new minor-onboarding path can clear or create safety records without strong checks around external data and durable persistence. Please make the Keycast status check strict, make the audit write part of a successful claim-link response, and attach underage-report work to the Durable Object lifecycle before this merges.

---
**Additional required changes**

- **Attach age-review side effects to the Durable Object lifecycle** ([worker/src/ReportWatcher.ts:633](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-relay-manager/blob/b9743d92c1f82fd63e7511fb6513e2331e5decec/worker/src/ReportWatcher.ts#L633))
  Attach `createAgeReviewCase` to the Durable Object work before `handleReportEvent` returns.
  The `NS-underageUser` branch starts Keycast and D1 work as an untracked promise, so the WebSocket handler can finish before the safety case is durably scheduled or written.
  Await the async path, register it with the Durable Object lifetime, or persist a small queue item before returning.
  Keep the pending-pubkey guard behavior and add a test that underage reports are not considered processed until the insert path is scheduled or complete.

comment.body:
Make the local audit write part of a successful minor-account response.
This path can create the Keycast account and one-time claim link, then swallow a D1 insert failure and still return `{ success: true, claim_url, case_id }`.
That leaves operators without the durable moderation record for an already-created minor account, and the recovery log includes the claim URL.
Reject malformed `zendesk_ticket_id` before calling Keycast, and if the D1 insert fails after Keycast succeeds, return a recoverable error or persist a recovery record without logging the claim URL.

@dcadenas Thanks for review. I pulled all the child-safety and underage aliases into shared/categories.ts and build HIGH_PRIORITY_CATEGORIES from that, so labels and high-priority handling stay in sync. Reports.tsx now imports the shared list instead of keeping its own copy, and ReportWatcher uses the same underage aliases for age-review cases. Added tests that assert high-priority membership for each alias. Should be ready for another look when you have a minute 🙏

review.body:
Several moderation actions can now do the wrong thing or skip required audit and relay confirmation. Please fix the inline issues before merge so restore, delete, and deletion-publish behavior stay safe.

---
**Additional required changes**

- **Restore media actions affect every hash on the event** ([src/components/EventActions.tsx:134](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-relay-manager/blob/c39b473cefc583edf6ee1e5d5145f56ab8e238bf/src/components/EventActions.tsx#L134))
  Filter restore actions to the hashes that actually match the selected state before sending `SAFE`.
  Right now this path loops over every media hash passed into `EventActions`, while `ReportDetail` passes all hashes and only aggregate flags.
  On an event with a restricted hash and a blocked hash, Remove Restriction can also unblock the blocked hash.
  Pass per-hash status or derive filtered lists so Unblock only clears blocked hashes and Remove Restriction only clears restricted hashes.
- **Profile delete path skips the moderation decision audit row** ([src/components/ReportDetail.tsx:794](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-relay-manager/blob/c39b473cefc583edf6ee1e5d5145f56ab8e238bf/src/components/ReportDetail.tsx#L794))
  Log the moderation decision before refreshing after this delete path.
  This callback now calls `deleteEvent` directly from the reported-user card, but the replaced mutation also wrote `moderation_decisions` with the report id.
  That lets a normal report-review delete remove relay content without the audit row tied to the report.
  Await `logDecision` with targetType `event`, action `delete_event`, the deleted event id, reason, and `reportId: report?.id` after `deleteEvent` succeeds.
- **Kind 5 deletion publishing uses the wrong relay transport** ([worker/src/nip86.ts:220](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-relay-manager/blob/c39b473cefc583edf6ee1e5d5145f56ab8e238bf/worker/src/nip86.ts#L220))
  Publish kind-5 deletion events through the relay event transport that waits for acceptance.
  This helper builds a normal Nostr `["EVENT", event]` frame but posts it with `fetch()` to an HTTP URL derived from `RELAY_URL`.
  Standard Nostr relays accept `EVENT` frames over WebSocket and return `OK`, so permanent delete can ban the event but fail to publish the NIP-09 deletion request.
  Use the existing WebSocket publish path or a documented HTTP ingestion endpoint with a test against that exact endpoint.
✅ Keycast and Zendesk fixes land cleanly

The child-safety alias change needs one canonical safety policy before merge.
Some accepted aliases can show the right label while still skipping high-priority handling.

comment.body:
Include every accepted child-safety and underage alias in the shared high-priority policy, and use that shared policy in `Reports.tsx` instead of a local copy.
Right now `CATEGORY_LABELS` accepts `childSafety`, `child-safety`, `NS-underageUser`, `NS-underage-user`, `underageUser`, and `underage-user`, but `HIGH_PRIORITY_CATEGORIES` only adds `NS-childSafety` and `NS-child-safety`.
A report with one of the missing aliases gets the friendly label while `HIGH_PRIORITY_CATEGORIES.includes(category)` stays false, so moderator-safety handling can miss media hiding, priority sorting, and badges.
Add tests that cover high-priority membership for each accepted child-safety and underage alias.

This service-binding path still hardcodes the moderation hostname instead of using `env.MODERATION_ADMIN_URL`.
The rest of the worker treats that config value as the source of truth, so a hostname change can break bulk delete, age-restrict, or un-age-restrict media calls again.
Build the service-binding `Request` from `${env.MODERATION_ADMIN_URL}/api/v1/moderate` and add a bulk-moderate test that sets a non-default URL and asserts the exact request URL.

review.body: ✅ bulk moderation host fix, one config suggestion inline.

issue.title: fix: dedup report categories, surface Keycast failures, audit partial deletes
issue.body:
## Summary

- **Dedup getReportCategory and HIGH_PRIORITY_CATEGORIES** (closes #81): the local copy in Reports.tsx was missing `NS-underageUser` and `NS-childSafety` (6 entries vs 8 in constants), so child-safety reports weren't getting priority treatment in the queue list. Now imports from `@/lib/constants`.

- **Surface failed Keycast enforcement in age review** (pre-existing): when a moderator restricts/clears/denies an age review case, the worker calls Keycast to suspend/unsuspend/ban the account and returns `keycastUpdated` in the response. The UI was ignoring this flag — showing success even when account enforcement failed silently. Now shows a destructive toast so the moderator knows to retry or escalate.

- **Audit partial deletes in combined event+media deletion** (pre-existing): the "Delete Event & Media" action ran four sequential steps with a single audit log at the end. If media deletion failed after the event was already destroyed, the error toast hid what succeeded and the audit trail was incomplete. Now logs each irreversible side effect as it completes and surfaces partial success to the moderator.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] All 99 tests pass (10 suites including EventActions and AgeReviewDetail)
- [ ] Staging: verify child-safety reports appear with priority badge in queue
- [ ] Staging: trigger age review restrict with Keycast unconfigured, verify warning toast appears
- [ ] Staging: verify combined delete surfaces partial success if media step fails

comment.body:
Thanks Daniel — both findings are real issues. They predate this PR (the dedup was the original scope) but I've addressed them here since they're straightforward to fix.

**Keycast enforcement (AgeReviewDetail):** The `AgeReviewCaseResponse` type now includes `keycastUpdated`. The mutation checks it on state transitions that trigger Keycast calls (restricted/cleared/denied). When `keycastUpdated: false`, a destructive toast tells the moderator account enforcement didn't apply and to retry or escalate. Commit: `9f0e5da`.

**Partial delete audit (EventActions):** `deleteEventAndMediaMutation` now logs a decision immediately after each irreversible side effect (event delete). On partial failure, it writes a `delete_event_and_media_partial` audit record listing what completed, and the error toast says "Partially completed" with specifics instead of a generic failure. The UI also calls `onActionComplete()` on partial success so the view refreshes to reflect the event being gone. Same commit.

review.body:
Two moderation paths need changes before merge: age-review enforcement failures must not look successful, and combined delete must preserve audit state across partial failure. Both are normal moderator actions, so the PR needs to make these failure modes visible and recoverable.

---
**Additional required changes**

- **Surface failed account enforcement** ([src/components/AgeReviewDetail.tsx:100](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-relay-manager/blob/070b21948b8eb2398e3a3cac76975abd4775b08b/src/components/AgeReviewDetail.tsx#L100))
  Treat `keycastUpdated: false` as a failed moderation action here.
  The worker can persist the case change and still return 200 when Keycast suspension or ban fails, so the UI currently tells the moderator the action worked while account enforcement did not happen.
  Show a retryable error, or change the API contract so required account enforcement failures fail the state transition.
- **Preserve audit state for partial deletes** ([src/components/EventActions.tsx:176](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-relay-manager/blob/070b21948b8eb2398e3a3cac76975abd4775b08b/src/components/EventActions.tsx#L176))
  Preserve an audit record as each irreversible side effect succeeds in this combined delete flow.
  The event delete and deletion-request publish can both complete before media deletion or the final decision log fails, which leaves the mutation in a failed state after moderation work has already happened.
  Log completed side effects immediately, or return a partial-success result that refreshes the UI and makes the audit trail explicit.

issue.title: task: wire age review actions to Keycast account suspension
issue.body:
## Context

Keycast PR #235 (account suspension) merged May 20. Keycast now exposes `GET/PUT /api/admin/users/:pubkey/status` with service-token auth. Status values: `active`, `suspended`, `banned`. Suspended users cannot sign events or decrypt DMs via the signer.

Relay-manager's age review system currently restricts accounts by age-restricting media (Blossom) and optionally banning the pubkey (Funnelcake). This is effective but imprecise: media restriction hides existing content, but the user can still post new events via any client that doesn't use Keycast signing. With Keycast suspension, the restriction is authoritative.

## What

When a moderator transitions an age review case to a restricted state (`restricted_pending_user_response`, `restricted_pending_support_email`):
- Call `PUT /api/admin/users/:pubkey/status` with `{ status: "suspended", suspended_reason: "age_review" }`

When a moderator clears the case (`clear`):
- Call `PUT /api/admin/users/:pubkey/status` with `{ status: "active" }`

When a case expires (cron auto-close with deny outcome):
- Keep suspended (no unsuspend call)

## Prerequisites

- `KEYCAST_SERVICE_TOKEN` secret set on relay-manager staging + production
- `KEYCAST_URL` env var (probably `https://login.divine.video`)

## Acceptance criteria

- Restricting an account in age review suspends the user in Keycast
- Clearing a case unsuspends the user in Keycast
- Keycast call failure does not block the age review state transition (graceful degradation -- log the error, continue)
- Integration test covering the suspend/unsuspend calls

## Related

- Keycast PR divinevideo/keycast#235 (merged)
- Relay-manager PR #78 (deletion alignment, in review)
- Under-16 coordination doc: `docs/moderation/under-16-system-coordination.md`

comment.body:
Fixed in b4b9f3e. Replaced `clearedRestrictedState` (which required the immediately prior state to be restricted) with an unconditional check on `requestedState === 'cleared'`. Both `unsuspendUser` and `un-age-restrict-all` are idempotent, so they fire on every clear regardless of prior state.

Added regression tests for `restricted_pending_*` → `submitted_for_review` → `cleared` and `needs_follow_up` → `cleared`.

review.body: The Keycast account state must be fixed before merge. Clearing an age review case can currently leave the account suspended after the case moves through review or follow-up states.

comment.body:
Make the clear transition unsuspend accounts that already passed through a restricted age-review state, not only accounts whose immediately previous state is restricted.
A normal path is `restricted_pending_*` -> `submitted_for_review` or `needs_follow_up` -> `cleared`, and the middle transition intentionally leaves Keycast suspended.
With the current `clearedRestrictedState` check, the final clear skips `unsuspendUser` and leaves the account suspended after the case is cleared.
Add a regression test for `restricted_pending_*` -> `submitted_for_review` -> `cleared`, and cover `needs_follow_up` if that path can also follow a suspension.
